title: Conjecture 1.1 (Burcroff)
statement_text: If $G = \prod_{i=1}^{n} K[u_i, t_i]$ is a direct product of balanced complete multipartite graphs, then $\alpha(G) = IR(G)$.
context_text: Burcroff observed that earlier proofs establishing $\alpha(G) = \Gamma(G)$ for the cases $t_n \leq 2$ and $n \leq 3$ (due to Defant and Iyer) did not use the dominating property, hence those cases actually give $\alpha(G) = IR(G)$. She then conjectured this equality holds in full generality, strengthening the original Defant–Iyer conjecture.
paper_contribution: Proves $\alpha(G) = IR(G)$ for all direct products of balanced complete multipartite graphs except at most 37 explicitly listed exceptional graphs $Z_1, \ldots, Z_{37}$.
paper_title: Isoperimetry, Stability, and Irredundance in Direct Products

title: Conjecture 1.2
statement_text: If $H_1, \ldots, H_n$ are complete multipartite graphs and $G = \prod_{i=1}^{n} H_i$, then $\alpha(G) = IR(G)$.
context_text: Graphs are simple. The direct (tensor) product $\prod_{i=1}^n H_i$ has vertex set $V(H_1)\times\dots\times V(H_n)$, two vertices $(g_1,\dots,g_n)$ and $(g'_1,\dots,g'_n)$ being adjacent if and only if $g_i g'_i\in E(H_i)$ for every $i$. A complete multipartite graph is balanced if all its parts have the same size. For $S\subseteq V(G)$, $N[S]$ is the closed neighbourhood of $S$; $S$ is irredundant if $N[S\setminus\{v\}]\ne N[S]$ for every $v\in S$, and the upper irredundance number $IR(G)$ is the maximum size of an irredundant set. Since every maximal independent set is an irredundant dominating set, $\alpha(G)\le\Gamma(G)\le IR(G)$, where $\Gamma(G)$ is the upper domination number. Motivated by unitary Cayley graphs of finite rings (which are direct products of balanced complete multipartite graphs), Defant and Iyer conjectured $\alpha(G)=\Gamma(G)$ for such products, and Burcroff conjectured the stronger $\alpha(G)=IR(G)$ for direct products of balanced complete multipartite graphs. The authors prove Burcroff's conjecture except for at most $37$ specific products, and show that for any direct product of $n$ (not necessarily balanced) complete multipartite graphs, $IR(G)\le\alpha(G)+2^n$. This conjecture removes the balancedness assumption.
paper_title: Isoperimetry, Stability, and Irredundance in Direct Products
